style: Say clearly and kindly, like a patient elementary school teacher
lines: Welcome to Code Tracer. A program runs one line at a time. Before each line runs, predict what it will do. Then run it and check.
Type your guess in the empty box, then press Run line.
It matched. You traced that line just like the computer would.
Not quite. Read the line again. The right side is worked out first, then stored in the variable on the left.
This line asks a question. Is it true? Tap Yes or No, then press Run line.
A repeat line runs the lines tucked under it again and again. Watch the round number.
Lines that start with a hash sign are notes for people. The computer skips them.
Now test the note. Does it tell the truth about what happened? Tap Yes or No on the note card.
Traced! Your table is a record of every step the program took.
Traced! Your table is a record of every step the program took. Press Next for a new program.
You traced all twelve programs. Press Workbench to change the numbers.
This is the Workbench. Tap a number in the code to change it, then press Step and watch the table.
The program is done. Press Restart to run it again, or tap a number to change it.
You changed the code. Notes don't change by themselves. Press Step, then check: is the note still true?
Here is what that line does. Next time, try a guess first.
Type a guess first, or press Just show me.
apples equals apples plus 2 takes the 3 already in apples, adds 2, and stores 5 back in apples.
Setting steps to 7 throws the 2 away. A variable holds only one value at a time.
coins plus coins is 6 plus 6. Both use the value coins holds right now.
b equals a copied the 4. When a changed later, b kept its own 4.
Use the newest value in each column. cats was 6 by then, so dogs becomes 7 plus 6, which is 13.
left got the 8 first, so the 3 was gone. Then right equals left copied 8 back.
Each round adds 1 to jumps. Four rounds, four more.
Each round doubles blocks: 1, then 2, then 4, then 8.
Each round, total adds the current n, then n goes up by one. 1 plus 2 plus 3 is 6.
temp is 75. Is 75 more than 80? No, so the line inside the if is skipped and fan stays 0.
The first if made points 18. So the second if sees 18, which is more than 15.
In round 4, lives is 0. Is 0 more than 0? No. So lives stops at 0.
Right. The note says swap, but both ended up 8. The code does not do what the note says. Press Next, or try Swap with a spare on the Workbench.
Look at the last row. left is 8 and right is 8. Did the 3 get swapped over? Press Next for a new program.
Right. total ended at 6, and 1 plus 2 plus 3 is 6. The note is true. Press Next for a new program.
Check the table. total ended at 6. What is 1 plus 2 plus 3? Press Next for a new program.
Right. Four rounds, but lives stopped at 0. The if kept it from going below 0. Press Workbench to change the numbers.
Look down the lives column. Did it ever go below 0? Press Workbench to change the numbers.
